target_customer: Freight forwarders, plus manufacturers and retailers with inbound shipments exposed to geopolitical disruption
problem: Wars, strikes and tariffs disrupt global shipping and freight teams lack early warning on which shipments are exposed and what to do.
business_model: B2B software and managed service for freight and inventory planning (pricing not public)

founders.name: Alina Park
previous_startups: Yachay AI (text-based geolocation system, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says founding engineer at Inca Digital and CFTC Innovator of the Year. Education not listed.

competitors.name: Everstream Analytics
competitors.what: Supply chain risk analytics and annual risk reporting

competitors.name: Maplecroft (Verisk)
competitors.what: Supply chain risk outlook covering critical infrastructure hubs, commented on the 2026 Hormuz crisis

technical_complexity.rationale: Forecasting escalation from over one million sources and mapping it to container-level exposure is hard, though the YC page gives no evidence of validation.

defensibility.rationale: Claimed forecasting engine and eight years of team escalation-prediction work, but no customers named and risk analytics incumbents exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unknown as of the research date, the company is a few months old.

market_need_then: The 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure and tariff volatility made supply chain disruption prominent in 2026 coverage; the company cites its own forecast of ceasefire dates during that event (self reported).

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and urgent; human plus AI accountability messaging on the site

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confusable with Ekho, a separate auto commerce company that raised a Series A in 2025, and no brand assets were found.

outcome_analysis: Ekho Labs is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founder reports eight years of escalation prediction work and the company says the product anticipated events during the 2026 Hormuz closure, but customers are unnamed and no funding is verified. The company website and YC page describe different emphases (geopolitical forecasting versus managed inventory planning), which suggests early positioning changes.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125k seed round, single aggregator, unverified, probably the standard YC deal. Do not confuse with Ekho (auto commerce, Series A 2025). A third party wiki says the site was later refocused on ocean freight, unverified.
